answer: Sybil resistance can be priced into the identity graph. A new identity is admitted only through an edge two parties co-sign after real interaction, so the honest core is a dense kernel of cheap, reused edges. A sybil must bridge in from outside, and each needs a co-signature from a party already carrying risk, so it pays stake, delay and exposure per edge. No one can forge a cluster of mutually vouching fakes: edge weight comes from independent corroboration, so a closed loop of fresh keys carries almost none and never settles. Cost scales with credible edges, not keys minted.
